cross_listing_check.note: Drivers, bridge, WACC, caps and weights are identical to the WB model; the only inputs that differ are price, quote currency and fx. The 9898.HK USD-basis values should therefore equal the WB values to rounding, and the HKD values should equal them x 7.8419. Any gap larger than engine-version rounding is an error in this file.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (0.8%), rounded; the base path averages ~0.75%/yr over 10 years
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (5.6%/6.9%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue CAGR (-1.5%/0.8%): book value compounds only because ~US$300-400M/yr of owner FCF is retained after US$150-200M of dividends, not because the business is growing. Equity CAGR is therefore rejected as the growth anchor. EPS 3-yr CAGR of 68% is an artefact of the FY2022 trough (investment impairments cut EPS to US$0.36) and is ignored.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs from research/9898.HK/Reports/9898.HK_Metrics.csv (USD millions, FY2020-FY2025; EPS in US$ per share). FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 553.9, FY2021 613.7, FY2022 303.8, FY2023 416.7, FY2024 385.4, FY2025 318.2 (margins 32.8% -> 18.1%). Owner-FCF 5-yr CAGR (-10.5%) is below reported FCF (-7.6%) because interest income rose over the period (US$86M -> US$117M) while operating cash generation fell; a rising share of reported FCF is now yield on the cash pile rather than platform cash flow. SBC, by contrast, has collapsed (6.1% of revenue in FY2022 to 2.4% in FY2025 and ~0.8% in H1 2026), which flatters the 3-yr owner-FCF CAGR (+1.6%).

scenario_narratives.base: Weibo is a mature, ex-growth public-square platform. Advertising (~85% of revenue) is roughly flat in USD terms: Alibaba (+49% in FY2025, +10% in Q2 2026) and resilient verticals (auto/NEV, local services, internet services) offset a shrinking ex-Alibaba advertiser base, VAS grows modestly, and reported revenue drifts from -1% to +2% a year through FY2035. The FY2026 step-down in operating margin (H1 26% vs 30%) from higher content, production and marketing spend to defend engagement is treated as permanent, with AI-driven eCPM gains preventing further erosion rather than restoring the old 35%+ adjusted EBITDA margin. Cash taxes ramp to 25% as dividend-repatriation withholding grows. The value is mostly balance sheet: net cash of US$0.76B plus haircut long-term investments and the SINA receivable are worth ~US$5.1 (~HK$40) per share before any operating cash flow is counted -- roughly 80% of the current HK$49 price.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2025-26 ad softness is cyclical, not structural. Chinese consumption recovers, the auto/NEV launch cycle and celebrity/entertainment marketing keep growing, Alibaba's shopping-festival spend continues to compound, VAS sustains double-digit growth and AI ad tools raise yield per impression, giving 3-4% revenue growth for five years. Defensive marketing spend normalises and adjusted EBITDA margin recovers to ~32% by FY2031. The US$200M buyback is executed at depressed prices (value-neutral in the model, but it funds the flat count) and the HK listing plus continued dividends keep the China discount from widening.
scenario_narratives.bear: Weibo's displacement from brand-marketing budgets is structural: Douyin, Xiaohongshu and WeChat Channels own discovery and conversion, the advertiser count keeps shrinking (0.6M -> 0.4M in one year), MAU attrition continues (567M FY2025, 561M Q2 2026), and a further CAC crackdown on celebrity-gossip content removes the engagement engine. Alibaba, now ~12% of ad revenue, redirects budget. Revenue falls ~25% by FY2033 and margin settles at 20%. The VIE/HFCAA tail (forced restructuring, US delisting with the HK line as the only venue -- which would also trigger the convertible's fundamental-change put) and further impairments of the RMB investment portfolio are the reasons this scenario carries a 35% weight rather than the house default 15%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Weibo is valued as a mature, cash-generative advertising platform on fully SBC-expensed owner FCF, with the interest and investment income stripped from the flows and the assets that produce them (net cash, long-term investments at a 50% haircut, the SINA receivable at 75%) added back in the bridge, minority interests deducted once, and the 2030 convertible treated as debt rather than as shares. The China/VIE premium is charged once, in an 11.5% USD cost of equity used across all scenarios; Weibo-specific operating risk is charged in the scenario paths and a 35% bear weight. Terminal values are capped at 12x (10x bear) owner FCF to avoid assuming a re-rating the stock has never had. The model is built in USD, the reporting currency, and converted to HKD at the pegged rate only for the per-share comparison with the 9898.HK quote; it is the same model as WB's and should tie to it. The gap between the resulting value and the HK$49 price is the market's China/VIE/structural-decline discount made explicit; the model does not pretend to know whether that discount closes, which is why the 15% hurdle entry price and the bear case are reported alongside the weighted value.
key_risks_to_valuation: VIE and HFCAA structure: HK and ADS holders hold a contractual claim, not equity in the PRC operating business; an adverse PRC ruling or US delisting is a tail the DCF cannot price except through the bear weight and the country premium. A NASDAQ delisting would leave 9898.HK as the only venue and trigger the convertible's fundamental-change repurchase right.

Balance-sheet value may not reach shareholders: ~US$5/share (~HK$40) of the value is net cash, RMB investments and a loan to the private parent; it depends on continued repatriation (5-10% withholding), the SINA receivable being collected, and the investment portfolio not being impaired further (H1 2026 already shows ~US$90M of non-operating losses).
Structural ad-share loss: advertiser count fell from 0.6M to 0.4M in one year; if ex-Alibaba revenue keeps falling 4%+ a year the bear path is the base path.
Alibaba concentration (~12% of ad revenue and rising) plus Alibaba's shareholder position: a budget reallocation would remove the one growing ad stream.
Margin compression continuing beyond FY2026 (content/production costs, CAC compliance burden) -- each 1pp of permanent EBITDA margin is roughly US$0.5-0.6 (~HK$4-5) per share.

RMB depreciation: USD-reported revenue was -4% constant-currency in Q2 2026 vs +2% reported; the growth path is in USD and inherits FX. The HKD/USD peg adds no further translation risk unless the peg moves.

Long-term-investment haircut judgment: 50% is a round-number view of an undisclosed mix; each 10pp is ~US$0.65 (~HK$5) per share. 'Other non-current assets' (US$1.25B) are excluded entirely, which may be too harsh.
Secondary-listing liquidity: 9898.HK volume is a fraction of WB's; the HK line can gap from ADS parity on thin days, and HKD holders receive a USD-declared dividend.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, HKEX regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range HK$48.10-91.00. USDHKD from Yahoo HKD=X at the date in inputs.fx_note. Parity-checked against WB (NASDAQ) closes either side of the HK close.
data_sources.financials: research/9898.HK/Reports/9898.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2019-FY2025 from the 20-F annual reports in research/9898.HK/Extracted/, USD millions; interest income, cash taxes, D&A, NCI and short-term investments from the kpis table); Weibo Q2 2026 6-K exhibit 99.1 (SEC accession 0001104659-26-098504, fetched and read 2026-10-24) for the 2026-06-30 balance sheet, H1 2026 income statement, share counts and SBC; 9898.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt for the debt instruments (term loan US$900M facility / US$800M outstanding, 2030 senior notes US$750M, 2030 convertible US$330M).
data_sources.qualitative: research/9898.HK/Reports/9898.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-24): business model, Alibaba concentration, CAC/regulatory history, VIE/HFCAA risk, Q2 2026 commentary, dividend cut and buyback authorisation. Prior house model: research/WB/Reports/WB_Drivers.json (2026-10-04).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F cash flow statement add-back (9898.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:11576, US$42,067 thousand). Weibo publishes no combined 'SBC incl. equity-award taxes' figure and no separate net-share-settlement tax line in financing activities (EquityAwardTaxes recorded as 0 by the financial-parser), so the add-back is used alone. H1 2026 SBC was US$6.6M (Q2 2026 6-K non-GAAP reconciliation), ~0.8% of revenue.
inputs.fx_note: Statements, flows and the DCF are in USD (Weibo reports in US$; the underlying economics are RMB, >98% PRC revenue, FY2025 translated at RMB6.9931/US$). The Hong Kong secondary listing quotes HKD, so per-share values are built in USD and converted at USDHKD 7.8419 (Yahoo HKD=X, 2026-10-23T20:20Z; the peg band is 7.75-7.85, so the rate is stable to within 1%). Direction: model (USD) -> quote (HKD), multiply. Parity check on the 1:1 cross-listing: 9898.HK HK$49.08 (2026-10-23 HKEX close, 08:08Z) / 7.8419 = US$6.26, between the WB NASDAQ closes of US$6.32 (2026-10-22) and US$6.20 (2026-10-23, after the HK close), i.e. the HK line trades within ~1% of ADS parity once the time-zone lag is allowed for. One ADS = one Class A ordinary share, so no ADS-ratio adjustment applies. Unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry prices are in HKD (quote currency) to be comparable with current_price; USD twins are the reporting-currency values and should tie to the WB model.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T08:08:08Z HKEX regular close (Friday); not an after-hours print. 52-week range HK$48.10-91.00, so the price is within 2% of its 52-week low.
inputs.share_count_basis: 246.0M = Q2 2026 basic weighted shares 239.46M (6-K) + ~6.6M dilutive options/RSUs. The 6-K diluted count of 271.55M also includes ~25M if-converted shares from the US$330M 2030 convertible notes (conversion price ~US$13 / ~HK$102 vs a HK$49 price); those notes are carried as DEBT at principal in total_debt, so they are NOT also added to the share count (a convert charged both ways is the share-count double-count). The CSV SharesOutstanding of 268.56M (FY2025) is the diluted weighted average on the same if-converted basis and is therefore not used as the divisor. Cross-check: 245.55M ordinary shares issued at 2025-12-31, which already contains the award-reserve shares, agrees within 0.2%. Count held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buyback_cash is 0 for FY2025 and H1 2026 (the only repurchase in the history is US$57.7M in FY2022; basic shares rose 238.6M -> 239.5M YoY), so the flat count is a modelling convention the US$200M authorisation running to end-2026 has not yet funded.
inputs.net_debt_note: Balance sheet at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 6-K exhibit 99.1, verified line by line 2026-10-24): cash US$1,639.1M + short-term investments US$997.4M = US$2,636.6M (restricted cash US$2.4M excluded). Debt at PRINCIPAL: US$330M 1.375% convertible senior notes due 2030 (carrying 325.5; holder put December 2027) + US$750M 3.375% unsecured senior notes due July 2030 (carrying 746.1) + US$800M SOFR+1.28% term loan due 2027 (US$900M facility fully drawn, US$100M repaid Q4 2023; carrying 795.8; the US$300M revolver was repaid and cancelled in Q3 2025) = US$1,880M; no short-term borrowings. Net debt = 1,880.0 - 2,636.6 = -756.6 (net cash). The FY2025 CSV TotalDebt of US$1,863.55M is the carrying value of the same three instruments (principal less unamortised issuance cost) and ties. Operating lease liabilities (US$42.4M at 2025-12-31) are excluded: US GAAP operating-lease cost sits inside opex/EBITDA, i.e. lease treatment (B), charged once in the flows.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD-reported, so the rate is USD-built: 10-yr UST ~4.1% + beta 1.1 x ERP 5.0% = 9.6%, plus a 2.0pp China country / VIE-structure premium (sovereign CDS spread plus the untested contractual-control claim and HFCAA overhang that apply to every PRC ADR / HK secondary listing, not to Weibo specifically) = ~11.6% cost of equity, rounded to 11.5%. The HKD quote does not change the rate: the HKD is pegged to the USD and the flows are USD anyway. No leverage credit is taken: the US$1.88B of bonds and loans is more than covered by US$2.64B of cash and short-term investments, so the firm is economically unlevered and WACC = cost of equity. Market-value weights would push WACC toward 6% only because the equity is depressed, which would be circular. Risk is charged ONCE: the discount rate carries the generic China/VIE premium; Weibo-specific operating risk (ad-share loss to Douyin/Xiaohongshu, CAC enforcement, Alibaba concentration, margin compression) lives in the scenario paths and the elevated bear weight. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: US GAAP operating-lease expense (US$13.0M cash paid FY2025) is already inside cost of revenue/opex and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path; lease liabilities (US$42.4M) are excluded from net debt. No lease_cost_pct_path is needed because the margin is anchored to post-lease-expense GAAP operating income.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled on a consolidated basis (EBITDA margin anchored to consolidated operating income), so the non-controlling interests are deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book: US$56.5M NCI + US$17.8M redeemable NCI at 2026-06-30 = -US$74.3M. NCI's share of net income is small (US$3.0M FY2025, US$0.8M H1 2026), so book is a fair proxy.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, consumer internet', plus the non-US adaptations file for the USD/HKD quote split, excluded income / matching assets, NCI and charge-risk-once). Weibo is an advertising-funded social platform (~85% ad / ~15% VAS); it is not a bank, REIT, holdco or distressed name, so no other route applies. CROSS-LISTING: 9898.HK is the 1:1 Hong Kong secondary line of WB (NASDAQ), which already carries a house model dated 2026-10-04 (research/WB/Reports/WB_Drivers.json, memory entry wb-weibo). This is the FIRST valuation of the 9898.HK ticker, so there is no reconciliation block, but it is NOT an independent re-derivation: every driver path, weight, haircut, WACC and cap is carried over from the WB model unchanged, and only the anchors differ (price, quote currency, fx rate, data-source pointers). Nothing has happened in the three weeks since the WB build that would move a driver -- no new filing (Q3 2026 results are due mid-November 2026), no guidance (Weibo does not guide numerically), and the only change is the price (WB US$6.33 -> US$6.20; 9898.HK HK$49.68 -> HK$49.08). UNCHANGED, DELIBERATELY: FY2026 growth +2% / margin 27.5% (would move on the Q3 2026 print: ad revenue was flagged to face 'certain pressure' from high comparatives, and a Q3 ad decline of more than ~5% or an operating margin below ~24% would pull the FY2026 and FY2027 rows down); FY2027-35 growth and margin paths (would move on evidence that ex-Alibaba advertiser attrition has stopped, or that Alibaba spend is being cut); SBC 1.2% -> 1.5% (would move if FY2026 grants re-accelerate; H1 2026 ran at 0.8%); cash tax 22% -> 25% (would move on an HNTE status change or a change in dividend-repatriation withholding); WACC 11.5%, caps 12x/10x, weights 35/45/20, LT-investment haircut 50% and SINA receivable 75% (would move on a disclosed impairment or a collection of the SINA loan). OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF 477.111 - SBC 42.067 - interest income 116.826 = 318.218 (18.1% of revenue). Interest income is stripped because the gross cash pile (US$2.64B) that earns it is added back in the bridge; FY2025 reported OCF is after ~US$75M of interest PAID on the bonds/loans (US GAAP), so the FY0 unlevered equivalent is ~US$378M (21.5%) -- the forward component build is unlevered and subtracts net debt, so the two are consistent; the year-1 component FCF (~US$330M, 18.4%) sits below that because the FY2026 margin compression (H1 2026 operating margin 26.3% vs 30.4%; Q2 28% non-GAAP vs 36%) is built in. EXCLUDED-INCOME / MATCHING-ASSET RULE: FY2025 pre-tax income of 605.6 vs operating income of 464.8 implies ~US$106M of interest, dividend and investment gains outside the operating flows; all of it is excluded from the forward build, so its source assets are brought into the bridge: long-term investments (US$1,602.8M at 2026-06-30: measurement-alternative private-company stakes, equity-method and available-for-sale preferred positions, all RMB-denominated and illiquid, with a record of impairments -- FY2022 pre-tax income fell to 128 on ~350 of investment losses, and H1 2026 pre-tax 142 vs operating 230 implies another ~US$90M of non-operating losses) taken at a 50% HAIRCUT (US$801.4M); and the US$440.3M 'Amount due from SINA' (interest-bearing loan to the private controlling shareholder) at 75% (US$330.2M) for related-party recoverability risk. Each 10pp on the long-term-investment haircut is ~US$0.65/share (~HK$5.1). 'Other non-current assets' of US$1,245.5M (long-term deposits/wealth-management products, deferred tax, long-term prepayments, ROU assets -- composition not disclosed in the 6-K) is NOT added: a deliberate conservative omission, since part of the stripped interest income probably comes from it. CONVERTIBLE: US$330M 2030 notes treated as debt (conversion ~US$13 vs US$6.26 parity price) and excluded from the share count; see share_count_basis. DIVIDEND: FY2025 dividend cut to US$0.61/share (~US$150M) from US$0.82; value-neutral in an FCF model but it lowers the cash yield a HKD holder receives (dividends are declared in USD). HORIZON: 10 years, because the base/bull margin paths are still moving in year 5 and the bear path only bottoms in year 5. TERMINAL CAP 12x (10x bear) per the method's 'structurally slower business' guidance -- Weibo has traded at 3-6x EV/EBITDA for five years and a 20x cap would be a re-rating bet. FY2026 GUIDANCE: none numeric; H1 2026 revenue US$875.2M (+4.0% reported, about flat constant-currency), Q3 ad revenue flagged to face 'certain pressure', so FY2026 base growth is +2%. HK-LINE SPECIFICS: thinner liquidity than the ADS and a HKD-denominated holder bears USD/HKD peg risk on a USD dividend; neither changes intrinsic value, and the expected tie is 9898.HK value = WB value x 7.8419 (see cross_listing_check).

bear.rationale: Structural: the SME advertiser base keeps leaving for Douyin/Xiaohongshu/WeChat Channels, MAU attrition continues, a further CAC enforcement round curbs the celebrity-gossip content that drives engagement, and Alibaba redirects budget. Revenue falls ~25% to ~US$1.31B by FY2033 and adjusted EBITDA margin settles at 20% because content and compliance costs cannot be cut as fast as revenue. Terminal growth 1%, cap 10x. Same WACC as base/bull (risk is in the flows and the weight, not stacked in the rate).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +2%: H1 2026 +4.0% reported (about flat constant-currency), Q3 ad revenue guided to 'certain pressure'. FY2027-28 -1%/yr as ex-Alibaba advertiser attrition (count 0.6M -> 0.4M, ex-Alibaba ad revenue -4% in FY2025) continues to outrun Alibaba and VAS growth; then stabilisation at 0-2% nominal as the platform settles into its entertainment/news/PR niche. Revenue in FY2035 ~US$1.89B, 8% above FY2025. Carried unchanged from the WB model of 2026-10-04.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA margin was 35-37% in FY2021-24 and 32.2% in FY2025; H1 2026 ~30% vs ~37% a year earlier and H2 2025 ~28%, so FY2026 lands near 27.5%. Held at 27% thereafter: the content/marketing spend needed to defend engagement is treated as permanent, with AI eCPM gains only offsetting further erosion.
base.sbc_rationale: FY2025 2.4%, H1 2026 0.8%. Anchored at 1.2% for FY2026 and normalised to 1.5% (some re-grant for retention after the collapse in award values); historical 4-6% is not re-assumed.
base.capex_da_rationale: D&A 3.3% (FY2025 3.36%); capex 2.8% (FY2024 3.5%, FY2025 2.4%, H1 2026 well under 1%). The gap is the amortisation of acquired intangibles, which is not replaced.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes FY2025 US$94.4M = 20% of EBIT; GAAP ETR 24% FY2025 and 27% H1 2026. PRC statutory 25% with HNTE 15% at some subsidiaries, plus 5-10% withholding on dividends repatriated to fund the dividend. Ramp 22% -> 25%.
base.wc_rationale: Ad-supported; deferred revenue flat at US$70-100M, receivables ~23% of revenue. With revenue roughly flat the working-capital change rounds to zero.

bull.rationale: Ad softness proves cyclical: Chinese consumption recovers, auto/NEV, local services and celebrity-marketing verticals keep growing, Alibaba spend keeps compounding, VAS sustains double-digit growth (+19% Q2 2026) and AI eCPM gains lift yield per user without MAU growth. Margin returns to the FY2021-24 range of ~32% adjusted EBITDA by FY2031 as defensive marketing spend normalises.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 35% because Weibo meets three of the method's named triggers: a single-regulator dependency (CAC has acted against Weibo in 2021 and September 2025 and its content rules bite directly on the engagement model), a growing single-customer concentration (Alibaba ~US$174M and +49% in FY2025 while everyone else shrank), and a VIE/HFCAA structural tail that the flows cannot express. Bull held to 20% because it needs two independent things to go right -- a Chinese consumption recovery AND a margin recovery to the FY2021-24 range -- and the advertiser-count data points the other way. Base 45%. Identical to the WB model; the listing venue does not change the probabilities.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
trip_reasons: Base case upside 211% with price in the upper half of the 10yr range (164%)

diagnosis.detail: Projected growth 1.0% exceeds the through-cycle revenue CAGR -0.1%

sanity_check.sanity_check_note: historical_table prices and multiples are inflated by scripts/sanity_check.py's known fx-direction bug (memory: sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug): the cached price series is already in HKD (quote_currency) but the script multiplies by fx_rate (USD->HKD, 7.8419) again before computing market_cap against USD-denominated equity/EBITDA/revenue, so pb/ev_ebitda/p_sales are inflated by fx_rate once and the printed FY-end price by fx_rate twice (e.g. FY2021 printed 1984.00 vs real HK$253.00). Hand-bridged (convert price to USD by dividing by fx_rate, then market_cap = price_usd * shares_outstanding against USD-million equity/ebitda/revenue): FY2021-25 real P/B 0.56-2.07x, EV/EBITDA 3.05-10.97x, P/Sales 1.07-3.29x. At the current price (HK$49.08 = US$6.26): P/B 0.43x, EV/EBITDA 2.36x, P/Sales 0.96x -- below the 5yr range, consistent with the stock trading near multi-year lows. At the base-case IV (HK$152.70 = US$19.47): P/B 1.33x, EV/EBITDA 9.73x, P/Sales 2.98x -- at/near but not beyond the 5yr historical highs (max P/B 2.07x, max EV/EBITDA 10.97x). Genuine pass on the DCF; the trip was a false alarm from the fx bug, not a real driver problem. No driver changes applied.
